description:
FILED s513 (Fable, 2026-10-10) from the USER's question while s513g (#2878) was in its bars: "We talked about doing shims for just small subs in modules. That needs to be version dependent for those modules, right? How can new versions of CPAN modules be handled?"

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY (s513g's design): an overlay is a per-module file of forward declarations (prototypes + export names) about BEGIN-installed subs the static parse cannot see; the REAL module (whatever version is installed) still runs and supplies every value.  So an overlay IS version-dependent in principle -- but only through the names and prototypes of a handful of subs, which change rarely -- and drift is already LOUD on three sides: (1) the merge rule: a prototype the real source declares differently from the overlay is an ERROR naming both files; (2) the ProtoCache key carries the module's bytes AND the overlay's bytes, so an upgraded module is re-read and re-merged at the first transpile after the upgrade; (3) the #2610 detector announces at run time any BEGIN-installed sub whose parse the compiler got wrong -- the instrument that found these names in the first place keeps watching the new version.  A name the new version no longer installs is a run-time 'undefined subroutine' if the program calls it (loud), and nothing at all if it does not.

WHAT THIS TASK ADDS (two small things, the second is the real answer):
(a) THE VERSION STAMP: each overlay names the module version its facts were read from in perl's own syntax -- `package File::Path 2.18;` (perl's `package NAME VERSION`), so the file stays plain readable Perl; the reader compares it with the installed module's STATIC $VERSION (a literal `our $VERSION = '2.20'` in the source, read by the same walk; a computed $VERSION = unknown, no comparison) and, when they differ, ANNOUNCES ONCE on stderr (`PCL: facts overlay for File::Path was written for 2.18; installed 2.20 -- its declarations are still applied; a conflict with the source is an error`) and applies the facts anyway (rule 12's effect-only boundary: refusing would break every program on a routine upgrade for facts that almost never move).  Guard rows in Pl/t/facts-overlay-01.t: equal versions silent; differing versions announce once and still apply; a computed version silent.
(b) THE LEARNED FACTS (the follow-up s513g files from its own range when the reader lands -- do them together or make this the second half): at a module's INSTALL into the module cache the runtime records the prototypes the module actually installed (the `%pcl-sub-prototypes` registry after its BEGIN phase) into the cache SIDECAR; the extraction reads that sidecar next time and merges it the same way as an overlay (an installed fact outranks a hand-written one; the detector keeps verifying).  Then the hand-written overlay is only the BOOTSTRAP for the first run of a module whose facts the parse cannot see, and a new module version re-learns its own facts on its first run.  The two are the same reader with a second source; the first is one afternoon, the second a session.

NOT this task: a per-version overlay FILE (File/Path-2.18.pm) -- more files, no gain; the stamp + the learned facts cover drift.
subject: FACTS OVERLAY, VERSION DRIFT (USER question 2026-10-10 02:20): an overlay states the module VERSION it was read from in perl's own syntax (`package File::Path 2.18;`) and the reader ANNOUNCES once when the installed module's static $VERSION differs -- never refuses; then the LEARNED-facts follow-up makes the facts self-updating
